name: Lamares
tagline: Westernmost village of the Marches, where the road climbs into the hills and nobody shouts.
ruler: Lugo "Cold-Eyes" Varden, the Warden, from the Warden's Hall.

threshold: the road beginning its climb into the hills

night: the North Fortress's fire in the mouth of the gorge

dawn: shepherds heading up to the High Pens
dusk: locals gathering at the Red Pot

winter: flocks brought down to the pens
charcoal mounds smoking through the snow
summer: shearing, the whole village at the High Pens
autumn: wax and honey packed for the caravan
charcoal camps moving to new ground

situations.name: Ambarra
descriptors: handprints renewed on the shrine walls

situations.name: Shearing
descriptors: the whole village at the High Pens

itself.title: The western edge
itself.text: Lamares is the last village before the wilderness thickens, and it is proud of holding the edge. Everything here is watchful, and people don't shout.

itself.title: Wool, wax, and charcoal
itself.text: Sheep, bees, and the charcoal camps keep Lamares alive. Wool and honey go east on the caravans. Charcoal prices are falling, undercut by Dravesa.

itself.title: The North Fortress
itself.text: Three miles north, a stone tower and palisade guard the gorge to the Stone Pillars orcs. Captain Seretta says the orc patrols are too organized, and that something has changed.

day: **Lugo Varden** hears a dispute at the Warden's Hall and says almost nothing.
A charcoal burner swears he heard his own name called from the northern woods.
Charcoal burners come in black to the eyes, and the village gives them room.
A shepherd drives a flock down from the High Pens early, looking north.
**1d4 militia** ride out toward the North Fortress.
**Old Dreban** comes down for food, wearing one of his masks.
night: The watch calls a password the party doesn't know.
Quiet talk at the Red Pot stops when strangers come in.
Charcoal burners swear they heard voices in the northern woods.
The North Fortress's fire burns in the gorge mouth, then goes out.
**Captain Seretta** rides in after dark to see the Warden.

response.watch: A village watch that calls passwords at night, under the Warden.
response.reinforcements: 12 militia under Captain Seretta at the North Fortress, 3 miles north.
response.strength_now: 12 at the North Fortress, plus a small village watch
response.strength: The one town still behaving like a garrison: watchful, quiet, and asking for better weapons.

locations.name: Warden's Hall
locations.look: A slate-roofed stone hall at the centre of the village.

labels.interior: Benches, tables, weapon racks, and a map of the region pinned to the wall, annotated with patrols.

locations.name: The Red Pot
locations.look: A two-storey timber inn on a fieldstone foundation.

labels.common_room: Low-beamed and smoky, with a fire always going. Quiet talk; no brawling tolerated.
labels.services: 8 small rooms upstairs. Mutton stew, honey-cakes, charcoal-roasted vegetables, dark ale. Prices pending OSRIC 3.0 table.

locations.name: The High Pens
locations.look: Stone-walled sheep enclosures on the hillside west of the village.

labels.custom: Shepherds take the watch in turn. Shearing in early summer is a village-wide event.

locations.name: Hive Gardens
locations.look: Rows of hive-boxes behind stone walls on the southern edge, among herb patches.

locations.name: Charcoal Camps
locations.look: Smouldering earthen mounds in the hills east and north, moved each season.

labels.proprietor: The charcoal burners, respected but kept apart.

locations.name: Old Dreban's Hermitage
locations.look: A hut uphill among twisted pines, half a mile out, hung with carved wooden masks.

locations.name: Shrine to Bandua
locations.look: A stone hearth-shrine by the village green, its walls carved with handprints.

labels.rites: Oath-taking, household blessings, defensive prayers. The fire never goes out; it is rekindled from the Warden's Hall hearth.

locations.name: The North Fortress
locations.look: A stone watchtower, palisade, and barracks at the mouth of a gorge, 3 miles north.

labels.readiness: Alert. The orc patrols have changed.

factions.membership: The militia families; 12 at the North Fortress.
factions.scheme: Better weapons and more men for the fortress.

trouble: The Stone Pillars orcs are suddenly organized, and have built a fortress, the Tor, crowned by a henge moved there by telekinesis.
Charcoal burners hear voices in the northern woods; the village calls it nerves.
Charcoal prices are falling, undercut by Dravesa.
Wool is excellent, but the cost of carrying it east keeps rising.
